The word ``immersion'' here denotes the inclusion of a full subcategory, with ``open'' meaning a sieve and ``closed'' a cosieve. A sieve is closed under taking the source of an arrow whose target belongs to it; a cosieve is closed under taking the target. In a poset these are, respectively, downward and upward closed subsets. This agrees with the conventions forced by the displayed examples. For a fully faithful $f$, the identity at $i$ is terminal in $f/f(i)$ and initial in $f(i)/f$. Let $A:[1]\to\Cat$ send $0$ to the point and $1$ to the discrete category $\{a,b\}$, with the transition selecting $a$. Its Grothendieck construction $X$ has three objects $u,a,b$, one nonidentity arrow $u\to a$, and projection $f:X\to[1]$ sending $u$ to $0$ and $a,b$ to $1$. The map $u\to a$ is a cocartesian lift of $0\to1$. The corresponding lift category is a point; the lift categories over identities have their identity lifts as initial objects. Thus $f$ is proper for every derivator under consideration.

The opening calculations make the geometric language of supports available before any homotopy theory is introduced. There is a documented reason for this starting point. In \emph{Pursuing Stacks}, \S69, Grothendieck traces his concern to the inadequacy of a single derived category for the trace and determinant formulas arising around SGA~5. The proposed replacement assigns a derived category to every diagram shape; filtered complexes and diagrams of triangles are instances of this larger construction. The opening calculations make the geometric language of supports available before any homotopy theory is introduced. There is a documented reason for this starting point. In \emph{Pursuing Stacks}, \S69, Grothendieck traces his concern to the inadequacy of a single derived category for the trace and determinant formulas arising around SGA~5. The proposed replacement assigns a derived category to every diagram shape; filtered complexes and diagrams of triangles are instances of this larger construction. The geometric terminology begins with a computational requirement. A right direct image over $y$ is initially computed on the comma category $X/y$. To compute it on the strict fibre $X_y$ instead, the inclusion $X_y\to X/y$ must be cofinal in the orientation appropriate to contravariant coefficients. Properness asserts this simultaneously for every $y$.

The small correction about posets is substantive but completely local. A category is a poset precisely when it is thin and skeletal: each Hom set has at most one member, and isomorphic objects are equal. Having only monomorphisms and no nonidentity isomorphisms does not imply thinness. The parallel-pair category printed in the editors' note is a counterexample, since every composable arrow that could test cancellation is an identity. No later construction depends on the incorrect characterization.
